Thank you for your patience. ::: :::: The original files in `_labs/lab3` are below: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_tree(path = "_labs/lab3/") ## _labs/lab3/ ## ├── app-api.R #<1> ## ├── app-api.py #<2> ## ├── eda-db.qmd #<3> ## ├── model-db.qmd #<4> ## ├── py-data-load.py #<5> ## └── r-data-load.R #<6> ``` ::: 1. R Shiny app 2. Python Shiny app 3. R EDA Quarto file 4. Python EDA Quarto file 5. Database connection via Python 6. Database connection via R In the previous labs, we build a Python model API with [`vetiver`](https://rstudio.github.io/vetiver-python/stable/) (I also repeated this [lab in R](https://rstudio.github.io/vetiver-r/)). This lab continues with accessing databases and using APIs. ## Comprehension questions ### Databases > ***1. Draw two mental maps for connecting to a database, one using a database driver (in a Python or R package) vs. an ODBC or JDBC driver. You should (at a minimum) include the nodes: database package, DBI (R only), driver, system driver, ODBC, JDBC, and database.*** #### Python In Python, there is a large database ecosystem (i.e., many driver options). ORM support with [SQLAlchemy](https://www.sqlalchemy.org/) and it's flexible (i.e., it can bypass standards if needed). ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'Python DB Connections' %%| fig-align: center %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'look': 'handDrawn', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace'}}}%% graph TB subgraph PyApp["Python App"] PyCode(["Python

System ODBC") JAVASys("Java Runtime
JVM/JRE") end subgraph DB["Database"] DBServ[("Database Server")] end %% Direct pathway (bypasses system layer) PyCode --> DBPkg DBPkg --> NatDrv NatDrv --"`Bypass System Layer`"--> DBServ %% ODBC pathway PyCode --> ODBCPkg ODBCPkg --> ODBCDrv ODBCDrv --> ODBCSys ODBCSys --> DBServ %% JDBC pathway PyCode --> JDBCPkg JDBCPkg --> JDBCDrv JDBCDrv --> JAVASys JAVASys --> DBServ style PyCode fill:#f3e5f5 style DBPkg fill:#e1f5fe style ODBCPkg fill:#fff3e0 style JDBCPkg fill:#e8f5e8 style DBServ fill:#4caf50,color:#fff ``` #### R In R, the **`DBI` package provides a universal interface** (same code works across drivers). This is a simpler model because all paths converge on `DBI` package. There is also better integration with R's data structures (i.e., `data.frame`s). ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'R Database Connection Pathways' %%| fig-align: center %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'look': 'handDrawn', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace'}}}%% graph TB subgraph "R App" A("R

JVM/JRE") end subgraph "Database" K[("Database Server")] end %% All paths go through DBI A --> B A --> C A --> D B --> E C --> E D --> E %% Direct pathway (bypasses system layer) E --> F F --"bypasses system layer"--> K %% ODBC pathway E --> G G --> I I --> K %% JDBC pathway E --> H H --> J J --> K style A fill:#f3e5f5 style E fill:#e1f5fe style B fill:#c8e6c9 style C fill:#fff3e0 style D fill:#e8f5e8 style K fill:#4caf50,color:#fff ``` **Both R and Python native database drivers bypass the system layer** and connect directly to databases. The system layer is only involved when using ODBC or JDBC connections. ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'DB Connection Mental Model Differences' %%| fig-align: center %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'look': 'handDrawn', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"16px"}}}%% graph TD subgraph "R Philosophy" A[DBI as Universal Interface] --> B[All paths converge to DBI] B --> C[Consistent API regardless of driver] end subgraph "Python Philosophy" D[DB-API 2.0 as Standard] --> E[Multiple competing approaches] E --> F[Choose best tool for job] end style B fill:#e1f5fe style E fill:#fff3e0 ``` ### APIs > ***2. Draw a mental map for using an API from R and Python. You should (at a minimum) include nodes for `{requests}`/`{httr2}`, request, HTTP verb/request method, headers, query parameters, body, JSON, response, and response code.*** In general, APIs are like the digital 'plumbing' that makes connections between modern software ecosystems possible. ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'APIs' %%| fig-align: center %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'look': 'handDrawn', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"16px"}}}%% graph LR DS["Data Scientist"] --> Req["API Request"] Req --> ApiServ["API Server"] ApiServ --> DataProcMod["Data Processing/Model"] DataProcMod --> Res["Results"] Res --> ApiServ ApiServ --> APIResp["API Response"] APIResp --> DS style ApiServ fill:#e1f5fe style DataProcMod fill:#f3e5f5 ``` APIs have standardized language that allows different software systems to communicate and share functionality (without needing to understand how the internal implementation works). **What do they communicate?** 1. What you can request (endpoints) 2. How to make the request (HTTP methods, parameters) 3. What you'll get back (response format) 4. When things go wrong (error codes) #### Python #### R > ***3. How can environment variables be used to keep secrets secure in your code?*** ### In lab 2 We previously turned our Python `scikit-learn` model into a `VetiverModel()`, saved it to a `pins` board, and then created a `VetiverAPI()`.[^lab2-with-py] - In R, we created a linear model (with `lm()` and `fastDummies`), converted it to a `vetiver_model()`, put it in a `board_folder()`, 'pinned' it with `vetiver_pin_write()`, then converted it into an API with `plumber::pr()` and `vetiver_api()`.[^lab2-with-r] [^lab2-with-r]: This can be found in [`_labs/lab2/R/model-vetiver-r.qmd`](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/tree/main/_labs/lab2/R/model-vetiver-r.qmd). [^lab2-with-py]: This can be found in [/_labs/lab2/model-vetiver/model-vetiver.qmd](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/blob/main/_labs/lab2/model-vetiver/model-vetiver.qmd) The sections below cover how to create and communicate with APIs. I've split each lab into separate `R/` and `Python/` folders and included RStudio project files. ## R App API The R App API files can be found in the [`_labs/lab3/` folder](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/tree/main/_labs/lab3/). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_tree(path = "_labs/lab3/") ## _labs/lab3/ ## ├── app-api.R ## ├── eda-db.qmd ## └── r-data-load.R ``` ::: ### eda-db.qmd {#sec-eda-db.qmd} The [`eda-db.qmd`](_labs/lab3/eda-db.qmd) file has the EDA R code from lab 1. It begins by loading the libraries: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(DBI) # add this library(duckdb) # add this library(palmerpenguins) # add this library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(dbplyr) ``` ::: The code below creates a connection to the database, but needs to be changed slightly so the `penguins` data is registered with `duckdb` (before the queries can be run). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # load penguins data first penguins_data <- palmerpenguins::penguins # then connect con <- DBI::dbConnect( duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = "my-db.duckdb" ) # register table duckdb_register(con, "penguins_data", penguins_data) # create table dbExecute(con, "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE penguins AS SELECT * FROM penguins_data") # create df df <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM penguins") |> na.omit() ``` ::: The table below displays the means of the measurements (body mass, flipper length, and bill length/depth) by species and sex: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df %>% group_by(species, sex) %>% summarise( across( ends_with("mm") | ends_with("g"), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE) ) ) %>% dplyr::collect() %>% knitr::kable() ``` ::: The graph displays the best-fit linear relationship between `bill_length_mm` and `body_mass_g` by `species`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df %>% ggplot( aes( x = bill_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species) ) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm") ``` ::: And we finish by closing the connection to the database. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} DBI::dbDisconnect(con) ``` ::: To view the original code in `eda-db.qmd`, expand the section below:
Expand to view eda-db.qmd ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```` --- title: "Penguins EDA" format: html: code-fold: true --- ## *Penguin Size and Mass by Sex and Species* ```{r} library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(dbplyr) con <- DBI::dbConnect( duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = "my-db.duckdb" ) df <- dplyr::tbl(con, "penguins") ``` ```{r} df %>% group_by(species, sex) %>% summarise( across( ends_with("mm") | ends_with("g"), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE) ) ) %>% dplyr::collect() %>% knitr::kable() ``` ## *Penguin Size vs Mass by Species* ```{r} df %>% ggplot(aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm") ``` ```{r} DBI::dbDisconnect(con) ``` ```` ::: :::
### app-api.R `app-api.R` creates an R Shiny application that calls the `vetiver` API. The top of the file creates an `api_url`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} api_url <- "http://127.0.0.1:8080/predict" ``` ::: #### UI The UI definition is below: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ui <- fluidPage( titlePanel("Penguin Mass Predictor"), # Model input values sidebarLayout( sidebarPanel( sliderInput( "bill_length", "Bill Length (mm)", min = 30, max = 60, value = 45, step = 0.1 ), selectInput( "sex", "Sex", c("Male", "Female") ), selectInput( "species", "Species", c("Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo") ), # Get model predictions actionButton( "predict", "Predict" ) ), mainPanel( h2("Penguin Parameters"), verbatimTextOutput("vals"), h2("Predicted Penguin Mass (g)"), textOutput("pred") ) ) ) ``` ::: #### Server The server definition is below: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} server <- function(input, output) { # Input params vals <- reactive( list( bill_length_mm = input$bill_length, species_Chinstrap = input$species == "Chinstrap", species_Gentoo = input$species == "Gentoo", sex_male = input$sex == "Male" ) ) # Fetch prediction from API pred <- eventReactive( input$predict, httr2::request(api_url) |> httr2::req_body_json(vals()) |> httr2::req_perform() |> httr2::resp_body_json(), ignoreInit = TRUE ) # Render to UI output$pred <- renderText(pred()$predict[[1]]) output$vals <- renderPrint(vals()) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server) ``` ::: ### r-data-load.R {#sec-r-data-load-r} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = "my-db.duckdb") DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "penguins", palmerpenguins::penguins) DBI::dbDisconnect(con) ``` ::: To view the original code in `r-data-load.R`, expand the section below:
Expand to view r-data-load.R ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = "my-db.duckdb") DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "penguins", palmerpenguins::penguins) DBI::dbDisconnect(con) ``` ::: :::
## Python App API The Python App API files can be found in the [`_labs/lab3/Python/` folder](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/tree/main/_labs/lab3/Python). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_tree(path = "_labs/lab3/Python/") ## _labs/lab3/Python/ ## ├── Python.Rproj ## ├── app-api.py ## ├── model-db.qmd ## └── py-data-load.py ``` ::: ### model-db.qmd {#sec-model-db} The [model-db.qmd](_labs/lab3/model-db.qmd) file contains the EDA from [lab 1](lab1.qmd). ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="false"} import duckdb from pandas import get_dummies import numpy as np from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression from sklearn import preprocessing ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="false"} con = duckdb.connect('my-db.duckdb') df = con.execute("SELECT * FROM penguins").fetchdf().dropna() con.close() df.head(3) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="false"} X = get_dummies(df[['bill_length_mm', 'species', 'sex']], drop_first = True) y = df['body_mass_g'] model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="false"} print(f"R^2 {model.score(X,y)}") print(f"Intercept {model.intercept_}") print(f"Columns {X.columns}") print(f"Coefficients {model.coef_}") ``` :::
Expand to view model-db.qmd ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```` --- title: "Model" format: html: code-fold: true --- ```{python} import duckdb from pandas import get_dummies import numpy as np from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression from sklearn import preprocessing ``` ## Get Data ```{python} con = duckdb.connect('my-db.duckdb') df = con.execute("SELECT * FROM penguins").fetchdf().dropna() con.close() df.head(3) ``` ## Define Model and Fit ```{python} X = get_dummies(df[['bill_length_mm', 'species', 'sex']], drop_first = True) y = df['body_mass_g'] model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y) ``` ## Get some information ```{python} print(f"R^2 {model.score(X,y)}") print(f"Intercept {model.intercept_}") print(f"Columns {X.columns}") print(f"Coefficients {model.coef_}") ``` ```` ::: :::
### app-api.py {#sec-app-api-py} `app-api.py` creates an Python Shiny application that calls the `vetiver` API. #### UI ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="false"} from shiny import App, render, ui, reactive import requests api_url = 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/predict' app_ui = ui.page_fluid( ui.panel_title("Penguin Mass Predictor"), ui.layout_sidebar( ui.panel_sidebar( [ui.input_slider("bill_length", "Bill Length (mm)", 30, 60, 45, step = 0.1), ui.input_select("sex", "Sex", ["Male", "Female"]), ui.input_select("species", "Species", ["Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"]), ui.input_action_button("predict", "Predict")] ), ui.panel_main( ui.h2("Penguin Parameters"), ui.output_text_verbatim("vals_out"), ui.h2("Predicted Penguin Mass (g)"), ui.output_text("pred_out") ) ) ) ``` ::: #### Server ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="false"} def server(input, output, session): @reactive.Calc def vals(): d = { "bill_length_mm" : input.bill_length(), "sex_Male" : input.sex() == "Male", "species_Gentoo" : input.species() == "Gentoo", "species_Chinstrap" : input.species() == "Chinstrap" } return d @reactive.Calc @reactive.event(input.predict) def pred(): r = requests.post(api_url, json = vals()) return r.json().get('predict')[0] @output @render.text def vals_out(): return f"{vals()}" @output @render.text def pred_out(): return f"{round(pred())}" ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="false"} app = App(app_ui, server) ``` :::
Expand to view app-api.py ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` from shiny import App, render, ui, reactive import requests api_url = 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/predict' app_ui = ui.page_fluid( ui.panel_title("Penguin Mass Predictor"), ui.layout_sidebar( ui.panel_sidebar( [ui.input_slider("bill_length", "Bill Length (mm)", 30, 60, 45, step = 0.1), ui.input_select("sex", "Sex", ["Male", "Female"]), ui.input_select("species", "Species", ["Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"]), ui.input_action_button("predict", "Predict")] ), ui.panel_main( ui.h2("Penguin Parameters"), ui.output_text_verbatim("vals_out"), ui.h2("Predicted Penguin Mass (g)"), ui.output_text("pred_out") ) ) ) def server(input, output, session): @reactive.Calc def vals(): d = { "bill_length_mm" : input.bill_length(), "sex_Male" : input.sex() == "Male", "species_Gentoo" : input.species() == "Gentoo", "species_Chinstrap" : input.species() == "Chinstrap" } return d @reactive.Calc @reactive.event(input.predict) def pred(): r = requests.post(api_url, json = vals()) return r.json().get('predict')[0] @output @render.text def vals_out(): return f"{vals()}" @output @render.text def pred_out(): return f"{round(pred())}" app = App(app_ui, server) ``` ::: :::
